anomaly_def.Name: CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description: Definition: Root cause located at the host CPU resource layer, where database-related processes consume an abnormally large and sustained share of CPU, leaving insufficient cycles for the rest of the workload. It is distinct from query-plan or workload anomalies because the diagnosis target is the saturation of the compute resource itself, regardless of which logical layer originally produced the demand. Observable phenomena: sustained host CPU utilization near saturation, elevated operating-system run queue and load average, increased context-switch rate, scheduler and runqueue wait events appearing in engine wait-event views, top statements concentrated by CPU time, and broad latency increases across otherwise unrelated statements once cores become saturated. Possible contributing factors: aggregate effect of inefficient queries, plan regressions, or missing indexes converging on CPU usage, excessive parallelism producing context-switch thrashing, maintenance or bulk-load jobs overlapping peak traffic, bind-value-sensitive plan reuse keeping a CPU-intensive plan in cache, tight application polling and connection-leak-driven active result sets, co-located services or noisy-neighbor virtual machines sharing physical cores, and undersized compute capacity relative to workload growth.

entry.official_definition: Specifies the amount of time with no network activity after which the operating system should send a TCP keepalive message to the client.
entry.trigger_condition: A TCP client connection has no network activity longer than tcp_keepalives_idle on systems supporting TCP_KEEPIDLE or an equivalent socket option.
entry.workload_impact: Starts TCP keepalive probing for an otherwise idle client connection; together with interval and count settings this can lead to dead connection detection.
entry.default_behavior: Default value is 0, selecting the operating system default.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
